_why: ADR 0050's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
The row worth re-deriving is C5, which is the only entry in this project
resolved by DELETING code rather than adding a test.
C5 removed `.replace(/\r?\n/g, " ")` and no test failed. The line was
dead: `\s` matches `\n` in JavaScript, so the `.replace(/\s+/g, " ")`
below it had always done the whole job. Deleting a dead line is right,
but it leaves a claim behind -- the ADR says the test was re-pointed at
the surviving mechanism and 'now fails 1 test'.
That claim is what C5R checks. If the re-point did not take, the
flattening would be untested and nobody would know, because the original
mutation can no longer be run against a line that no longer exists.

mutations.description: remove the SURVIVING flattener (the re-pointed C5)
mutations._claimed: 1 failed, after C5's dead line was deleted and the test re-pointed
mutations._note: A note containing a newline would otherwise emit a bare data row into the middle of the `#` header, and pandas would read it as data.

mutations.description: missing provenance reads as resolved rather than unknown
mutations._note: `origin ?? "unknown"`. A parameter with no provenance entry must not read as resolved -- the same rule as ADR 0029's `unstated` not being `wild_type`.
